title: Tec-11 Results Presentation Final.pptx
doc_type: technical results deck (pptx, 18.6 MB, ~19 slides; text rendering only, figures dropped)
issuer_author: IFR/Tonalli (IFR template "TSX-V: IFR | OTCQB: IFRTF", appendix divider reused from "Corporate Presentation July 2018"); drafts by GRE (Gavin Elsley) and CAH exist
summary: Post-drilling, pre-completion TEC-11 results deck. Slide order inferred from the text (rendering has no slide numbers): s1 regional Tampico basin/Golden Lane; s2 Tecolutla PSDM map with TEC-11 (A-A', 800 m scale); s3 seismic traverse TEC-5 area to TEC-7; s4 producing-wells structural cross-section (TEC-3 lowest oil test, TEC-2 2nd lowest oil test, TEC-6 lowest oil production, TEC-10 lowest oil show, TEC-11 landing, 70 m / 20 m annotations); s5 3D view NE of top El Abra with OWCs (TEC-10 deepest oil, TEC-10 Zone C oil, TEC-2 oil, PEMEX OWC); s6 TEC-10 summary "High porosity reef margin found in TEC-10 upper zone", "TEC-10 excellent reservoir"; s7 TEC-10 Interval C daily test chart; s8 TEC-2 analogue (Perf-1 to Perf-4, 316 kbbl since 1972); s9 TEC-11 build-section correlation; s10 TEC-11 proposed completion intervals 1-10 (plug-and-perf); s11 TEC-10 natural fracture identification ("FMI"); s12 TEC-11 uphole Tantoyuca potential; s13 thank you; s14 appendix divider; s15 3D view "PEMEX OWC 90 m lower than TEC-11 planned perfs"; s16 TEC-2 cuttings/facies table; s17-18 TEC-11 striplogs; s19 TEC-10 seismic tie to DMI-enhanced PSDM.
key_data_with_units: TEC-10 Interval C daily test 2018-09-20 to 2019-01-21 (124 values, axis to 2019-01-25): oil 2.4 -> peak 231.6 bbl/d (2018-10-20) -> 133.4 bbl/d; water 57.6 -> 70.4 (min) -> 128.0 bbl/d; total fluid 60 -> 344 (max) -> 261 bbl/d; gas 21 -> 314.7 (max) -> 111.7 Mcf/d; tubing pressure 153 -> 1,072.5 psi (2018-10-06) -> 504.6 psi. Monthly from the same series: Oct 2018 180.9 bbl/d oil, WC 42.1 %, Ptbg 875 psi; Jan 2019 141.1 bbl/d, WC 48.6 %, Ptbg 527 psi. Cum oil of the series 19,132 bbl ("over 19,000 bbl"). Post-stimulation flowback 1,475 bbl oil. TEC-2 cumulative 316,000 bbl since 1972 (Perf-1 to Perf-4). TEC-2 cuttings 2,326-2,340 m: white/cream limestone, partly cryptocrystalline, partly dense, isolated light-brown oil stains ("possible tidal channel"); 2,340-2,357 and 2,357-2,370 m: white to cream limestone, medium-coarse granular (microcoquina) of cemented miliolids in calcareous matrix, very isolated light-brown oil stains ("back reef to lagoon"). TEC-11: limestone at 2,611 mMD "like TEC-2"; reef-lagoon facies at 2,670 mMD; striplog 2,720-2,830 mMD; 10 proposed completion intervals.
interpretation: The TEC-10 test chart is the same data as the repository daily sheet (tecolutla_tec10_daily.csv, from the 2023 economics Tec-10 Prod sheet): identical on 2018-10-20 (231.6 bbl/d oil, 78.3 bbl/d water, 176.4 Mcf/d, 771.5 psi; WC 25.3 %, GOR 762 scf/bbl) and the 124-day sum is 19,132 bbl in both. Claims that do not hold: (1) "stable oil cut and high flowing pressures" - WC rose 42 -> 49 % and Ptbg fell 875 -> 527 psi (monthly) within the deck's own window, then WC reached 67 % in year one; (2) "high-porosity reef margin in TEC-10 upper zone / excellent reservoir" - the upper zone (2,270-2,311 mSS) reads 4-5 ohm.m and is water on the core-supported porosity (G-47); (3) "natural fractures throughout the El Abra on FMI", "open fractures critically stressed" - the tool is a CMI (G-09) and the repository picks no open fracture in the window or in the perforated 10 m, open fractures only below 2,320 mSS; (4) "successfully drilled, cased TEC-11 ... multiple completion intervals" - overtaken: liner hanger damaged, tie-back failed, acid could not be isolated, 100 % water; lateral 4-12 m below the TEC-6/9 high in mostly mudstone-wackestone (G-27, G-28); (5) "TEC-11 encountered a similar section to TEC-2" - not supported by the mud log (no pure grainstone, 31 m shale at 2,584-2,615 mMD, bentonite to TD); "limestone at 2,611 mMD" sits inside the logged shale interval - check; (6) Tantoyuca "upside" with oil show - the Aug 2019 Tantoyuca test made trace 17 API oil and 96 bbl/d water; (7) "PEMEX OWC 90 m lower than TEC-11 planned perfs" - no number; every well watered out within a year at 2,303-2,332 mSS and TEC-3 recovered water with oil at its lowest test (LKO -2,374.2 mSS). Supported: TEC-3 lowest oil test, TEC-6 lowest production interval, TEC-2 316 kbbl since 1972 (repository 328,146 bbl for the 2,307-2,311 mMD interval including about 10 kbbl Tonalli-era oil), 1,475 bbl flowback.
use_in_presentation: TEC-10 test history slide (daily chart s7 as a reusable figure); TEC-11 "what we said vs what happened" slide; seismic/structure figures s2, s3, s5, s19 (the only seismic displays available while G-55 is open; images must be extracted from the native pptx); TEC-2 facies table s16 for the facies slide
repo_impact: confirms: TEC-10 daily test data, 1,475 bbl flowback, peak 232 bbl/d on 2018-10-20, Oct 2018 181 bbl/d, TEC-2 cum ~316-318 kbbl since 1972, TEC-2 2,326-2,340 mMD cuttings (TAN s2). contradicts (IFR claims superseded by repository): TEC-10 upper-zone quality (G-47), FMI/open fractures (G-09), TEC-11 success and facies (G-27, G-28), Tantoyuca upside. adds: seismic image set for G-55 (images only, no SEG-Y); briefing A5 says "131 bbl/d at 49 % (Sep 2018)" - in this series 131-133 bbl/d at 49 % WC is 2019-01-19 to 01-21, while Sep 2018 averaged 101 bbl/d at 63 % WC (clean-up): check the briefing date

title: Tec-11 Results IFR IDESA_GRE.pptx
doc_type: technical deck re-issued for IDESA (third party) by GRE
issuer_author: IFR / GRE (Gavin Elsley, per the GRE conflicted-copy name)
summary: 2022 re-issue of the TEC-11 results for IDESA. Adds to the Jan 2019 deck: PSDM map labelled "El Abra aquifer" / "El Abra oil" around TEC-10, "Huge aquifer with a relatively small oil reservoir"; "Tec-2 production down to 2,335 m SSTVD"; "3 types of porosity in El Abra: intergranular, fractures, karst"; top El Abra map showing planned TEC-11 (320 deg azimuth) intersecting natural fractures predicted from TEC-10, SHmax 80 deg, critically stressed conjugate fault set, contour interval 20 m, 2,300 mTVDss; "Faults and fractures connect aquifer to oil column"; "Ancient karst is very high permeability and allows the aquifer to be recharged quickly and give pressure support"; conclusions as in the July 2019 meeting deck plus "Natural fractures could have been enhanced by acid stimulation".
key_data_with_units: TEC-2 and TEC-10 producing oil and water from 2,305-2,316 mTVDss; TEC-11 perfs producing water from 2,316-2,322 mTVDss; original free-water level 2,380 mTVDss; possible current FWL ~2,316 mTVDss with a transition zone above; TEC-2 production down to 2,335 mSSTVD; TEC-11 azimuth 320 deg; SHmax 80 deg.
interpretation: The operator's own post-mortem: TEC-11 was steered to cut critically stressed fractures that, by the same deck, connect the aquifer to the oil column, and the unisolated acid job probably opened them. The "risen FWL ~2,316 m with a transition zone above it" hypothesis puts the TEC-12 window (2,294-2,311 mSS) in the transition zone, which matches the repository's low-resistivity reading (G-47). "Huge aquifer, relatively small oil reservoir" is IFR's own words for the review's framing. Depths are on the By Zone/TVDss basis (TEC-10 2,311.5-2,315), not the survey basis adopted in G-46.
use_in_presentation: Drive mechanism / OWC slide (quote "huge aquifer, relatively small oil reservoir"; FWL 2,380 -> ~2,316 hypothesis); TEC-11 lessons slide (fracture-targeting azimuth plus unisolated acid); TEC-12 risk slide (window in a possible transition zone)
repo_impact: confirms: aquifer drive and pressure support (review section 2.4); TEC-11 water from 2,316-2,322 mTVDss consistent with liner perfs 2,674-2,745 mMD; TEC-11 azimuth (316-331 deg on the survey). adds: a fourth OWC/FWL figure (original FWL 2,380 mTVDss) for briefing B1.2, within ~6 m of TEC-3 LKO -2,374.2 mSS; the fracture-conduit / risen-FWL hypotheses bear on G-47 and on briefing A4 (coning vs flat rise); "TEC-2 production down to 2,335 mSSTVD" is consistent with the 1956-72 2,331-2,335 mSS interval

title: Tonall Strategy Meeting - Tec 11 Results Final July 13.pdf
doc_type: strategy meeting deck (PDF, 3.7 MB, ~15 pages; text layer read)
issuer_author: Tonalli / IFR ("Strictly confidential"; cover residue "Operational Strategy and Planning November 10th, 2016")
summary: TEC-11 results after the June-July 2019 completion and acid job. Pages (inferred from text order): p1 cover; p2 regional; p3 PSDM map "oil reservoir situated above a huge aquifer" (El Abra oil / El Abra aquifer around TEC-10); p4 seismic traverse TEC-5 to TEC-7; p5 3D top El Abra with OWCs; p6 producing-wells cross-section TEC-3, -7, -2, -6, -9, -10 with -2,300/-2,320/-2,340 m depth lines; p7 TEC-11 build-section correlation (TEC-101, -11, -2; TEC-2 production down to 2,335 m SSTVD); p8 completion programme; p9-10 striplogs; p11 three porosity types (intergranular, fractures, karst - Cave of the Swallows analogue); p12 top El Abra map with planned TEC-11 at 320 deg vs SHmax 80 deg and critically stressed conjugate faults; p13 top El Abra seismic depth with "possible current FWL" and "original FWL"; p14 TEC-11 testing compared with TEC-10; p15 observations and conclusions.
key_data_with_units: TEC-10 2018 unloading: unloaded with N2; no measurable oil until >1,100 bbl water produced (15-20x load fluid); flowback on 12/64 in choke; water pH 7, 19,000 ppm Cl. TEC-11 (to 2019-07-12 07:00): not unloaded with N2; ~935 bbl water produced = 1.5-2x load fluid; 12/64 in choke; only trace oil; water pH 7, 78,000 ppm Cl on 2019-07-10 ("still spent acid being produced"). Conclusions: TEC-2 and TEC-10 producing oil and water from 2,305-2,316 mTVDss; TEC-11 producing water from perfs at 2,316-2,322 mTVDss; either the regional FWL has risen from 2,380 to ~2,316 mTVDss with a transition zone above it, or water comes up fractures from a high-permeability aquifer; TEC-7 water probably via fractures.
interpretation: Primary source for the operator's July 2019 diagnosis. Two points matter for the presentation: (a) at the time of the meeting TEC-11 had returned only 1.5-2x its load fluid and was still producing spent acid (78,000 ppm Cl vs 19,000 ppm for TEC-10 formation water), while TEC-10 itself needed 15-20x load before it showed oil, so the July 2019 read of TEC-11 was not yet conclusive; the later 286 bbl/d 100 % water liner test and the Tantoyuca recompletion settled it; (b) the operator already suspected in 2019 that the zone above ~2,316 mTVDss could be a transition zone, which is the G-47 problem for TEC-12. The 19,000 ppm Cl TEC-10 water matches the 19,000-22,000 ppm field salinity column of the 2018 flowback and the Stiff analysis (Cl 20,850 mg/l); 78,000 ppm Cl is new.
use_in_presentation: TEC-11 lessons slide; OWC/FWL slide; TEC-12 risk slide (transition-zone hypothesis); figures p3, p6, p12, p13 (PDF small enough to pull natively)
repo_impact: confirms: TEC-10 water salinity (~19,000-21,000 ppm Cl), TEC-11 water-only result, TEC-7 water problem (briefing A5), aquifer support. adds: TEC-11 flowback 935 bbl water by 2019-07-12 at 1.5-2x load and 78,000 ppm Cl spent acid; TEC-10 >1,100 bbl water before oil (not in repository); original FWL 2,380 mTVDss; operator transition-zone hypothesis relevant to G-47; fracture-azimuth design rationale for TEC-11 (SHmax 80 deg, well at 320 deg). G-55: the PDF (3.7 MB) is the most practical source of the seismic/structure figures
